narrative:
The model estimated a 59.6% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that is above the 50% threshold, your application was denied. This is a probability-based decision, not a determination that you cannot succeed.

The strongest influence on the prediction was your undergraduate GPA of 3.30. Although it is close to the accepted-student average of 3.23, it was the top-ranked factor and, in your case, pushed the estimate toward failure. The second most important factor was your third-year class decile of 9, compared with an accepted-student average of about 5.8. This was a favorable signal and pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to outweigh the other factors. Your LSAT score of 40 was the third most influential factor and added to the failure side of the prediction.

To move forward, ask admissions whether an appeal or reconsideration process exists. Provide any evidence of bar-exam readiness, such as strong practice-test results, a structured study plan, or completion of a bar preparation course. Consider delaying enrollment until you can strengthen the areas reflected in this decision, and seek advising on how to demonstrate improvement. If possible, reapply with updated academic or test information and a clear plan for first-year bar success.
